## Problem and result

Explain the concrete CPU-scheduling or documentation problem and what changes for Lertick users. Keep the proposal within the current CPU-only scope.

## Evidence and validation

List primary sources, commands run, and results. Label estimates and hypotheses. Include raw data for any performance claim and explain tests not run.

## Compatibility, safety, and licensing

For kernel-facing changes, identify kernel/config/toolchain, load and recovery results, resource bounds, and SPDX/provenance. For documentation changes, note any status or interface changes. Phase 2 implementation requires explicit approval.
